Synopsis:
Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin signals uncertainty about whether further rate hikes will be necessary to return inflation to the 2% target. He sees transitory drivers (tariffs, oil, AI buildout demand) that may naturally ease, suggesting current restrictive rates could be sufficient. However, he flags upside risks: entrenched inflation since 2021, potential supply chain persistence, prolonged AI investment, and de-anchoring of inflation expectations. Markets currently price rates on hold in September, with hikes possible in October or December.
